einzeiler: How to handle too many client inquiries when your side hustle is growing fast
kurzfassung: A successful interior design business owner feels overwhelmed by receiving new client inquiries almost every day while being booked out for months. Host Chris Guillebeau advises implementing business systems, setting designated hours for correspondence, and using AI to triage messages. He also suggests charging for initial consultations to filter out less serious leads while crediting the fee toward future contracts.
stichpunkte: Kristen launched an interior design service earlier in the year and is now booked out for two months
She receives a new inquiry almost every day and feels overwhelmed by the heavy workload
Chris Guillebeau recommends improving business systems and establishing standard operating procedures
Batching communication by setting a specific weekly time for correspondence prevents constant interruptions
Virtual assistants or AI tools like Claude or Google Gemini can help triage initial inquiries
Charging for initial consultations reduces lead volume while filtering for higher-quality prospects
Consultation fees can double as a deposit that applies to the final contract if the project moves forward

clips.hook: Booked out for months with daily inquiries
clips.text: The caller shares that her interior design venture launched recently, secured two months of advance bookings, and continues generating daily project requests.

clips.hook: Using AI instead of hiring assistants
clips.text: The host explains that artificial intelligence tools can replace virtual assistants for filtering initial client messages to save money.

beschreibung:
Today’s caller has a different sort of problem than most people who struggle to get off the ground: her business is going so well that she’s feeling overwhelmed with the work.
